instrument_note: Reference chart and execution venue differ by basis. Store both separately and do not use reference levels as exact execution orders without basis adjustment.
state: Price UP + CVD UP strongly + OI FLAT with first post-CPI reclaim of dVAL
interpretation: This is materially healthier than the prior post-capitulation re-leveraging bounces. Aggressive buy flow surged while OI stayed almost unchanged, so the rebound is not being driven by a large new leverage build. Price also moved back above dVAL on the reference series after the CPI liquidation wick. The main caution is efficiency: CVD repaired much more strongly than price, so the reclaim still has to hold; if price cannot stay above dVAL despite the CVD surge, that becomes buyer-inefficiency and failed-reclaim evidence for a short setup.

basis_note.warning: Basis is dynamic; recalculate before execution.

long_scenario.trigger: Hold/retest above dVAL ~77.065k reference (~76.90-76.95k execution at current observed basis) while CVD remains firm and OI does not expand pathologically.
long_scenario.add_confirmation: Reclaim/accept above dPOC ~77.365k reference, then dVAH ~77.505k.
long_scenario.invalidation: Lose dVAL again with CVD rolling over; stronger invalidation if price falls while OI begins to expand.

short_scenario.trigger: Price falls back below dVAL after this strong CVD recovery, forms a lower high/rejection, and CVD stalls/turns down while OI remains flat/up.
short_scenario.interpretation: That would convert the current bullish-looking flow into buyer inefficiency and recreate the failed-reclaim short edge.
short_scenario.avoid: Do not short solely because CVD is high; the current structural reclaim must fail first.

lesson: Post-news recovery quality is higher when price and CVD recover without a simultaneous OI surge. However, a large CVD improvement that cannot hold reclaimed value is especially informative: the same data can flip from long confirmation to buyer-inefficiency short evidence. Track both structural acceptance and flow efficiency.
